I made the branch `feat/google-analytics` and added the Google tag to `app/index.html`. It isn't committed yet.

- **Where it goes:** inside `<head>`, right after the charset and viewport tags. Google suggests putting it straight after `<head>`, but the page's character encoding should be declared first. The tag is still near the top of the head, so this makes no practical difference.
- **Formatting:** Prettier reformatted the snippet to match the project's style (double quotes, multi-line function). It behaves exactly the same.
- **Security headers:** `app/public/_headers` has no Content-Security-Policy, so nothing will block the Google script and the headers didn't need changing.

**Checks:**
- **Production build:** passes, and the measurement ID is in `app/dist/index.html`.
- **Typecheck and knip:** pass.
- **Lint:** 0 errors and 26 warnings. The warnings are Tailwind class warnings in component files I didn't touch.
- **Format check:** `npm run verify` reports a failure, but `index.html` itself passes. The failure comes from the build output in `app/dist/`, which was already there before my build. Prettier is run from `app/`, and there's no `.prettierignore` there to exclude it. Adding `dist` to an `app/.prettierignore` would fix it if you want.

**Decision for you:** the tag also loads when you run the local dev server, so your own testing will show up in Analytics. I can limit it to production builds with a small Vite plugin. The other option is to filter out local traffic inside GA.

Want me to commit it as `feat(analytics): add Google Analytics gtag`?

```typescript
import { defineConfig, loadEnv, type Plugin } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";

const GA_MEASUREMENT_ID = "G-3JZRV3QZRD";

// Injects the Google tag (gtag.js) into production builds only, so the dev server isn't tracked
function googleAnalytics(id: string): Plugin {
  return {
    name: "google-analytics",
    apply: "build",
    transformIndexHtml: () => [
      {
        tag: "script",
        attrs: {
          async: true,
          src: `https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=${id}`,
        },
        injectTo: "head-prepend",
      },
      {
        tag: "script",
        children: `window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
gtag('js', new Date());
gtag('config', '${id}');`,
        injectTo: "head-prepend",
      },
    ],
  };
}

export default defineConfig(({ mode }) => {
  const env = loadEnv(mode, __dirname, "");
  return {
    plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), googleAnalytics(GA_MEASUREMENT_ID)],
    server: { port: Number(env.PORT) || 5173 },
  };
});

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-30 07:46:13Z)**_

The Google tag now only goes into production builds; the dev server no longer loads it. This change isn't committed yet.

**What changed:**
- **`app/vite.config.ts`:** a small `googleAnalytics()` plugin adds the tag only when you run `vite build`. The measurement ID `G-3JZRV3QZRD` is now defined once, as a constant in this file.
- **`app/index.html`:** I removed the tag from here, so it can't load in dev by accident.

**Checks:**
- **Production build:** the tag is the first thing inside `<head>` in `app/dist/index.html`, which is where Google recommends it. The charset tag now comes after it but is still well within the first 1024 bytes, which is where browsers need to find it.
- **Dev server:** I started it, fetched the page, and found no Google tag. Then I stopped it.
- **Lint, Prettier, typecheck, knip:** all pass on the changed files.

`npm run preview` serves the production build on your machine, so visits there will still be tracked. Pages preview deployments on `*.pages.dev` will be tracked too. If you want those excluded, I can add a hostname check so the tag only runs on `chromacurve.style`.

Should I commit it as `feat(analytics): inject gtag in production builds only`? I'd stage only `app/vite.config.ts` and `app/index.html` and leave the `.specstory` files and `AGENTS.md` out.

````text
## (1) `transformIndexHtml`

**Description:** "Dedicated hook for transforming HTML entry point files such as `index.html`."

**Type:** "`IndexHtmlTransformHook | { order?: 'pre' | 'post', handler: IndexHtmlTransformHook }`"

**Signature:** The full type begins with "`type IndexHtmlTransformHook = (`" and ends with "`Promise<IndexHtmlTransformResult | void>`". The `ctx` parameter includes `path`, `filename`, `server?`, `bundle?`, `chunk?`, and `originalUrl?`.

**Return values:** "An array of tag descriptor objects (`{ tag, attrs, children }`) to inject to the existing HTML."

**`HtmlTagDescriptor`:**
- `tag: string`
- `attrs?: Record<string, string | boolean>` with the comment "attribute values will be escaped automatically if needed"
- `children?: string | HtmlTagDescriptor[]`
- `injectTo?: 'head' | 'body' | 'head-prepend' | 'body-prepend'` with the comment "default: 'head-prepend'"

The docs list the four `injectTo` values but do not explain each one.

**Order:** "In order to inject a script that should go through the Vite plugins pipeline," followed by "`order: 'pre'` will apply the hook before processing the HTML." Also: "`order: 'post'` applies the hook after all hooks with `order` undefined are applied."

**Examples:** The docs have no example that injects tags. The only example replaces the title:

```js
const htmlPlugin = () => {
  return {
    name: 'html-transform',
    transformIndexHtml(html) {
      return html.replace(
        /<title>(.*?)<\/title>/,
        `<title>Title replaced!</title>`,
      )
    },
  }
}
```

## (2) Conditional Application (`apply`)

"By default plugins are invoked for both serve and build."

"use the `apply` property to only invoke them during `'build'` or `'serve'`:"

```js
function myPlugin() {
  return {
    name: 'build-only',
    apply: 'build', // or 'serve'
  }
}
```

"A function can also be used for more precise control:"

```js
apply(config, { command }) {
  // apply only on build but not for SSR
  return command === 'build' && !config.build.ssr
}
```

The docs do not give a formal `'build' | 'serve' | function` type. They show string values and a function example.

None. The page does not mention deprecating `enforce`/`transform` in favor of `order`/`handler` for `transformIndexHtml`. The `order` option is presented as the current form, and `enforce` appears only in the Plugin Ordering section.
````

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-30 07:47:52Z)**_

Yes, I checked it against the official Vite docs (the v8.3.4 docs, which are current) and against the type definitions for the version you have installed.

- **Officially recommended for this job.** The Vite env-and-mode guide says Vite is "intentionally unopinionated about complex replacements like conditionals" in `index.html`. For that kind of logic it points to "a custom plugin that implements the `transformIndexHtml` hook," which is what I wrote. Vite has no built-in way to include HTML in one mode and leave it out in another. The `%VITE_X%` substitution can only fill in values; it can't remove the `<script>` tag in dev.
- **The APIs are current and supported.**
  - `apply: 'build'` is the documented way to run a plugin only for `vite build`.
  - Returning an array of tag descriptors (`{ tag, attrs, children, injectTo }`) from `transformIndexHtml` is documented and isn't deprecated.
  - `injectTo: 'head-prepend'` is a documented option, and it's actually the default.
- **It matches your installed version.** You have Vite 7.3.1, and its type definitions have the same `HtmlTagDescriptor`, `injectTo` and `apply` signatures. The plugin uses the same API in Vite 7 and 8, so it won't need changes when you upgrade.

**Alternatives I ruled out:**
- **Loading the tag from `main.tsx` when `import.meta.env.PROD` is true:** works, but the tag wouldn't load until the JS bundle runs. Google recommends putting it in `<head>`.
- **Third-party plugins** (such as `vite-plugin-radar`): they'd add a dependency to replace about 20 lines of code.
- **GA4's internal or developer traffic filters:** these can be added on top in the GA admin. They don't stop the tag from loading in dev.

Two things to mention:
- I wanted to look this up in Context7 first, as your instructions say, but it isn't signed in. I can start its OAuth flow if you want it available for future lookups.
- You have Vite 7.3.1, but your preferred tooling lists Vite ^8. That's outside this change; the plugin works the same on 8.
